contributions.detail: 147 Form A rows over pp2-8 sum to 34,227.25, which is 2,065.00 MORE than the printed anchor of 32,162.25. The difference is the FILER'S OWN page-subtotal arithmetic and is traced exactly: the seven printed page subtotals (5,880.00 + 3,056.00 + 4,146.25 + 3,825.00 + 4,450.00 + 7,955.00 + 2,850.00) sum to 32,162.25, i.e. the grand total is the sum of the filer's subtotals, not of the filer's rows. Two subtotals under-count their own sheets. (i) p6 'Subtotal page 5 of 7' prints 4,450.00 against 25 rows that sum to 4,750.00 - short by exactly one 300.00 row; all three 300.00 cells on that sheet (rows 1, 15, 23) were re-cropped at 900dpi and each verifiably reads 300.00, and the printed subtotal cell itself verifiably reads 4,450.00, so which of the three the filer's SUM range dropped cannot be determined FROM THE PAGE - the most likely reading, by analogy with the p7 defect below, is that the SUM range began at row 2 and omitted row 1 (Mary Evans, 300.00). (ii) p7 'Subtotal page 6 of 7' prints 7,955.00 against 26 rows that sum to 9,720.00 - short by exactly 1,765.00, which is the sum of that sheet's FIRST THIRTEEN rows (Sharon Lewis 100.00 through Yaeko Bryner 100.00); rows 14-26 alone sum to 7,955.00 exactly. Those first 13 rows are the ones typed with the figure inline as '$100.00' in a single cell instead of in the split '$ | amount' cells used by rows 14-26, so the filer's SUM range plainly started at row 14. Nothing was nudged: every row is the printed figure and the delta is left standing as the filer's arithmetic.
